| ESS-025 — Informational independence and diversity of assurance evidence | Unsafe acceptance caused by correlated evidence error, common specification defects or organisational confirmation bias. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Informational independence and diversity of assurance evidence. | Disagreements, common inputs, oracle diversity, defect yield, challenge closure and configuration coverage. | The independent function needs organisational freedom and information access, but informational independence must be assessed separately. | One direct authoritative discriminator suffices when it conclusively decides a local reversible claim; reviewer multiplication adds no information. |
| ESS-026 — Claim–argument–evidence safety assurance | Unjustified operation or certification when the argument omits a hazard, rests on false premises or cites stale evidence. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Claim–argument–evidence safety assurance. | Evidence validity, claim coverage, assumptions, challenge status, operational indicators and configuration/change events. | The case owner must not control all challenge; acceptance authority needs power to reject or demand evidence. | A direct deterministic proof/test and a brief recorded rationale may be the whole case for a narrow reversible claim. |
| ESS-027 — Defeaters, counterevidence and authorised challenge in assurance | Loss after a plausible counter-scenario, adverse test or invalid assumption was ignored or normalised. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Defeaters, counterevidence and authorised challenge in assurance. | Open objections, negative tests, anomaly trends, premise failures, response quality and whether decisions changed. | Challengers need access and non-retaliation; decision authority must answer rather than merely receive objections. | For a settled low-consequence deterministic claim, one sanity check is enough; adversarial boards add no value. |
| ESS-028 — Configuration identity binding for safety evidence | Unsafe release or operation based on valid historical evidence that no longer describes the actual system. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Configuration identity binding for safety evidence. | Build/component IDs, calibration, parameters, environment, evidence version, deployment inventory and deviations. | Release/operations authority must be able to block unknown or mismatched configurations. | For a local disposable reversible experiment, identify only the artefact and conditions necessary to reproduce the decisive check. |
| ESS-029 — Safety impact analysis and proportionate re-assurance after change | Loss from changed behaviour or assumptions; or safety debt/workarounds caused by excessive change burden. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Safety impact analysis and proportionate re-assurance after change. | Diff/configuration identity, changed assumptions, affected tests, operational telemetry, regression and rollback readiness. | Change authority must be able to stop release, demand wider evidence and approve bounded reuse. | A trivial local reversible change with a decisive regression discriminator uses that check and records only the necessary identity. |
| ESS-030 — Living, current and operationally connected assurance | Operation continues under stale assurance that no longer represents current hazard exposure or control health. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Living, current and operationally connected assurance. | Configuration, control health, incidents/precursors, assumption monitors, evidence expiry and operational-envelope excursions. | Owners need authority to restrict, degrade, rollback or re-assure on adverse evidence. | Static assurance can suffice for a stable, bounded, short-lived and readily observed system; update only when a relevant trigger occurs. |
| ESS-031 — Independent assessment and IV&V where consequence warrants | Undetected systematic defect, optimistic interpretation or conflicted acceptance in consequential systems. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Independent assessment and IV&V where consequence warrants. | Independent defect findings, evidence provenance, unresolved dissent, retest results and configuration coverage. | The assessor must be able to report to an authority that can change design, release or operation. | Routine peer review or one deterministic check is sufficient for low-consequence reversible work; separate IV&V should not trigger by label alone. |
| ESS-032 — Evidence triangulation and targeted formal verification | Unsafe acceptance after untested corner states, invalid formal assumptions or common evidence blind spots. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Evidence triangulation and targeted formal verification. | Proof obligations, model assumptions, code/configuration correspondence, test coverage and operational anomalies. | Assurance authority decides where proof/test diversity is necessary and owns residual model risk. | Use direct execution, inspection or deterministic testing when it fully settles a simple claim; formalisation must earn its cost. |
| ESS-033 — Joint safety–security analysis for cyber-physical control | Physical or health loss caused or amplified by compromised digital/organisational control. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Joint safety–security analysis for cyber-physical control. | Security events, control/feedback integrity, patch/configuration status, availability, anomalies and attack-path assumptions. | Safety and security owners need a joint escalation/acceptance path; neither may unilaterally break the other control objective. | Do not impose a full threat programme on an isolated trivial reversible function with no plausible adversarial safety pathway. |
| ESS-034 — Actionable hazard detection and alarm burden control | Uncontained hazard due to missed, late, stale, ambiguous or ignored warning; secondary loss from needless stops. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Actionable hazard detection and alarm burden control. | Detection probability/latency, false/nuisance rate, acknowledgement, action completion, alarm floods and sensor health. | The receiver needs authority and resources to diagnose, stop, isolate or escalate; alarm ownership must be explicit. | Direct physical prevention or immediate observation may be cheaper than alarms; do not alert when no safe action exists. |
| ESS-035 — Containment, isolation and emergency stop with state confirmation | Hazard propagation after prevention fails | Protection system and authorised operator | Hazardous physical/software process and its energy/material/control paths | On trigger, propagation shall be interrupted and the contained/safe condition confirmed within the available time | Independent actuator/process state, residual energy/material and barrier integrity | Stop authority may be broad; restart authority must be distinct and evidence-based | Direct stop plus immediate observation for a local reversible process |
| ESS-036 — Context-sensitive fail-safe, fail-operational and graceful-degradation design | Loss caused either by hazardous continued operation or by removal of a service necessary to protect life/mission. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Context-sensitive fail-safe, fail-operational and graceful-degradation design. | Mode, remaining capability, environmental demand, barrier health, time in degraded state and operator comprehension. | Automation and operators need defined transition/override authority; degraded operation must have an accountable expiry/recovery owner. | For noncritical reversible functions, stop cleanly and recover normally; elaborate degradation architectures are unnecessary. |
| ESS-037 — Recovery, rollback and restart only after restored safety constraints | Recurrence or new loss during premature restoration | Recovery and restart authority | Stopped, isolated, degraded or modified system | The system shall return to service only after relevant constraints, configuration and observability are restored or residual risk is explicitly accepted | Configuration, barrier status, diagnostics, staged performance and recurrence indicators | Service restoration authority and safety restart acceptance must be explicit and may be separate | Direct verify-and-retry for a trivial reversible action |
| ESS-038 — Bounded emergency or temporary risk acceptance with compensating controls | Loss while a known protection is unavailable or while an exceptional configuration accumulates unexamined risk. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Bounded emergency or temporary risk acceptance with compensating controls. | Time/exposure, compensating-control health, changed conditions, incidents, handoffs and restoration progress. | A named emergency/risk authority must own the decision; operators need stop authority if compensation degrades. | Do not create a waiver for trivial work already inside ordinary authority, and do not use temporary acceptance to avoid feasible permanent correction. |
| ESS-039 — Incident, near-miss and precursor reporting connected to learning | Repeated or escalating loss because precursor evidence was suppressed, fragmented, misclassified or never consumed. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Incident, near-miss and precursor reporting connected to learning. | Report volume and exposure denominator, severity/precursor linkage, time to triage/action, repeat events, closure quality and reporter feedback. | Reporting recipients require authority or an escalation path; reporters need protection from inappropriate retaliation while reckless conduct remains separately governed. | For an immediately observed trivial defect already corrected and deterministically verified, a lightweight record or no separate report may be appropriate. |
| ESS-040 — Multi-factor causal investigation grounded in local rationality | Recurrence because upstream design, feedback, workload, authority, incentives, interfaces and defences remain unchanged. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Multi-factor causal investigation grounded in local rationality. | Timeline/state reconstruction, alternative explanations, missing/stale feedback, goal conflicts, control deficiencies, action implementation and recurrence. | Investigators need independence and access; organisations must empower consumers to change upstream controls rather than only retrain operators. | A simple, directly observed and deterministically reproducible defect can be corrected without an elaborate sociotechnical investigation. |
| ESS-041 — Corrective-action ownership, implementation and effectiveness verification | Repeat loss because recommendations have no capable consumer, address symptoms, are not implemented or create new hazards. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Corrective-action ownership, implementation and effectiveness verification. | Implementation evidence, changed control performance, recurrence/precursors, side effects, overdue status and reason for closure. | The owner must control resources/design/operations or have escalation; the investigator should not declare effectiveness solely from paperwork. | For a trivial directly fixed defect, the repair plus decisive regression check can close the action without a separate tracker. |
| ESS-042 — Leading indicators tied to explicit hazards and control performance | Latent degradation and migration toward hazard boundaries remain invisible until a severe event. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Leading indicators tied to explicit hazards and control performance. | Barrier availability, overdue proof tests, excursions, workload/override patterns, weak signals, exposure and decision response. | An owner must be able to inspect, restrict, maintain or redesign on adverse trends and to retire misleading indicators. | Use direct control-state inspection when available; do not create proxy metrics where a deterministic discriminator already answers the question. |
| ESS-043 — Organisational control, incentives and production-pressure analysis | Catastrophic loss arising from normal organisational adaptation, resource choices and authority/information failures. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Organisational control, incentives and production-pressure analysis. | Staffing/workload, deferred maintenance, waivers, schedule overrides, unresolved findings, reporting quality, barrier health and escalation outcomes. | Leaders controlling resources and priorities must own safety consequences; frontline responsibility requires matching authority. | Do not invent culture programmes for a simple local technical defect; correct the direct mechanism and verify it. |
| ESS-044 — Supplier and contractor boundary assurance with change notification | Loss from hidden component behaviour, interface mismatch, counterfeit/substituted part, evidence opacity or divided authority. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Supplier and contractor boundary assurance with change notification. | Supplier versions, deviations, anomalies, process/evidence changes, interface conformance and field performance. | The integrator must retain system-level acceptance authority; suppliers need authority/resources to disclose and correct defects. | Commodity low-consequence components with a decisive acceptance test can use that test rather than imposing a full supplier safety system. |
| ESS-045 — Operational monitoring and adaptive safety-envelope governance | Loss from envelope excursion, unobserved degradation, novel context or adaptation that invalidates prior assurance. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Operational monitoring and adaptive safety-envelope governance. | Envelope variables, assumption validity, control effectiveness, anomalies, drift, exposure and recovery performance. | Operations must have stop/degrade authority; adaptation outside the assured envelope requires explicit change/risk authority. | Stable bounded systems with direct deterministic protection may only need periodic checks; continuous dashboards are unnecessary. |
| ESS-046 — Cheap authoritative discriminator for low-consequence reversible work | Indirect safety loss from delayed repair/service, attention dilution and procedural noncompliance; wasted cost without improved discrimination. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Cheap authoritative discriminator for low-consequence reversible work. | Check result, exact local configuration, rollback success if used and evidence that assumptions did not widen. | Ordinary engineering authority may act within bounded delegation; anyone detecting scope expansion can escalate. | This property is itself the cheap path; it does not apply when consequence, irreversibility, coupling, latent effects or uncertain interactions are material. |
| ESS-047 — Retirement of controls whose hazard or decision consumer has disappeared | Safety attention dilution, alarm fatigue, workaround, unavailable service or false belief that an obsolete control remains protective. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Retirement of controls whose hazard or decision consumer has disappeared. | Consumer use, action triggered, false-positive/bypass burden, control effectiveness, dependencies and post-retirement anomalies. | The control owner and affected risk/operations authority must approve removal; users need a path to reveal hidden dependence. | Do not run a retirement review for a transient local check that naturally ends with the task. |
| ESS-048 — Live decision consumer for every safety artefact and control | Uncontrolled hazard masked by document completion, plus attention/cost displaced from effective controls. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Live decision consumer for every safety artefact and control. | Decision made, challenge raised, action/acceptance changed, use frequency, stale age and unresolved consumer feedback. | The consumer must be able to act or escalate; the producer cannot substitute document delivery for control. | Do not create a separate artefact when the decisive information is already embedded in an authoritative engineering/operational control. |
| ESS-049 — Hazard-control hierarchy favouring elimination and engineered control | Preventable exposure or catastrophic demand on humans/procedures after a feasible stronger control was omitted. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Hazard-control hierarchy favouring elimination and engineered control. | Hazard presence, barrier demand, human/procedural dependence, bypass, exposure and side effects of stronger controls. | Design/risk authority must be able to reject administrative substitution for feasible engineering control. | No hierarchy exercise is needed when the hazard is absent or a simple direct constraint already eliminates it. |
| ESS-050 — Safety margins, operating envelopes and boundary separation | Abrupt transition into an unrecoverable hazardous state after small variation, delay or latent degradation. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Safety margins, operating envelopes and boundary separation. | Distance to limit, uncertainty, rate of approach, ageing/degradation, excursions, recovery time and barrier availability. | Operators/controllers must be able to reduce demand, stop or degrade; change authority owns margin allocation. | For a low-consequence reversible state with immediate deterministic feedback, ordinary tolerance checks may suffice. |
| ESS-051 — Explicit assumption validity and monitoring | Unsafe behaviour outside the analysed context, common-mode failure or false assurance caused by premise drift. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Explicit assumption validity and monitoring. | Premise status, environmental range, interface/provider behaviour, data drift, independence evidence and violations. | Assumption owners and operators must be able to restrict use, escalate or change the case when validity is uncertain. | Do not create a register for obvious transient facts already enforced by a deterministic check; record only assumptions whose failure changes a decision. |
| ESS-052 — Durable current hazard, constraint and decision state | Known hazard reappears or remains uncontrolled because organisational memory and decision status are stale or fragmented. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Durable current hazard, constraint and decision state. | Control/evidence status, owner/acceptance, configuration, open scenarios, incidents, changes and review/expiry dates. | Hazard/control owners and acceptance authority must be named; unresolved hazards cannot disappear through administrative closure. | A local ephemeral hazard fully eliminated and verified can be recorded in the ordinary work item; a dedicated log is unnecessary. |
| ESS-053 — Integrated verification that a safety control achieves the intended state | Hazard remains or recurs despite nominally verified requirements and components. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Integrated verification that a safety control achieves the intended state. | Trigger, command, timing, actuation, process state, feedback semantics, degraded modes and post-control stability. | Verification authority needs access across component/organisational boundaries and power to block acceptance. | A single local direct test suffices when the control path is simple, fully observable and reversible. |
| ESS-054 — Safety management of lifecycle transitions and temporary configurations | Loss during transition, test, construction, maintenance or retirement when normal controls are absent or roles/configurations are ambiguous. | The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property. | The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise. | The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Safety management of lifecycle transitions and temporary configurations. | Temporary configuration, barrier availability, sequence/hold point, personnel/authority, tests, residual energy/material and exit criteria. | A transition controller must have cross-boundary authority and explicit handoff/hold-point release; normal operations authority may be insufficient. | Routine local reversible transitions with an established direct check use the ordinary procedure and observation. |


Every full `SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE`, including delay, over-application and mature form, is embedded in the property ledger and machine-readable JSON.

## EVOLVED_SYSTEMS_SAFETY_HAZARD_ANALYSIS_METHOD_LEDGER

No single technique is admitted as universal. Selection is driven by causal representation, decision value and proportionality.

| METHOD | LINEAGE | REPRESENTS | SYSTEMATIC_LIMITS | ASSUMPTIONS | DECISION_VALUE | MINIMUM_USEFUL_IMPLEMENTATION | COMPLEMENTS | FULL_RITUAL_UNNECESSARY_WHEN | SOURCES |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FMEA/FMECA | RELIABILITY_ANCESTRY | Bottom-up component/function failure modes, local/end effects, detectability/criticality and control actions. | Weak for hazardous interactions without component failure, multi-component timing/order, organisational control and unknown functions. | Decomposable functions/components, meaningful failure modes and knowledgeable analysts. | Design robustness, diagnostics, test/maintenance priorities and interface questions when findings have owners. | Hazard-relevant scope, credible modes/effects/controls and closed actions; no mandatory worksheet format. | System hazard analysis, FTA/common-cause analysis, STPA/scenario analysis and HAZOP where applicable. | One simple failure/control path is deterministically tested and reversible. | S005; S006; S007 |
| Fault-tree analysis (FTA) | RELIABILITY_ANCESTRY / CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING | Top-down logical combinations leading to a defined undesired event; can support cut sets and quantification. | Depends on top-event/boundary and event logic; dynamic, software, organisational and unknown interaction causes may be omitted. | Events and dependence are representable; probabilities/configuration are credible when quantified. | Architectural vulnerabilities, common paths, prevention priorities and sensitivity. | A decision-relevant top event, explicit logic/dependencies and action on dominant/critical paths. | FMEA, event trees, common-cause analysis, STPA/HAZOP, scenario and operational evidence. | A direct deterministic guard eliminates the top event or a simple causal chain is already established. | S008; S009 |
| Event-tree analysis (ETA) | RELIABILITY_ANCESTRY / DOMAIN_TRANSLATION | Forward sequences after an initiating event, including success/failure of protection and consequence branches. | Initiators, branch order, dependence and human/organisational adaptation are analyst-defined; tree growth can be severe. | Meaningful sequence/branch model and defensible branch probabilities if quantified. | Emergency/mitigation layer design, consequence pathways and preparedness. | Only branches that change controls or acceptance, with dependence and uncertainty visible. | FTA, barrier analysis, PRA, HAZOP and recovery analysis. | A single directly observed response path settles the consequence. | S096; S040 |
| HAZOP | PROCESS_SAFETY_LINEAGE | Departures from design intent using guidewords across process parameters, procedures, software or operations. | Guideword anchoring, workshop fatigue, weak probability treatment and limited assurance of interaction/organisational completeness. | Stable intent/parameters, multidisciplinary operating knowledge and empowered action closure. | Process/design changes, safeguards, operating procedures and test/monitoring actions. | Focused nodes/intent, disciplined deviation prompts and traceable closure. | LOPA/bow-tie, FTA/ETA, FMEA, common-cause and organisational/control analysis. | The system lacks process-like intent/deviation semantics or a direct check settles the hazard. | S010; S011; S094 |
| Preliminary, subsystem, system and operating hazard analyses | DIRECT_SYSTEM_SAFETY_LINEAGE | Lifecycle search from early loss/hazard framing through subsystem/interface/system/operational hazards and control allocation. | Can become generic list-making, duplicate logs and stale analyses; quality depends on boundary, expertise and integration. | Hazard taxonomy and lifecycle system knowledge mature over time; findings feed design and operations. | Early architecture, requirement/constraint allocation, verification, acceptance and operational controls. | Only analyses needed to expose distinct lifecycle/interface/operational hazard classes, linked to decisions. | All method-specific analyses selected by causal coverage. | A low-consequence local task has no distinct lifecycle/system interaction burden. | S012; S013; S014; S015; S016 |
| STPA | CONTROL_THEORETIC_REFORMULATION | Unsafe control actions, missing/inadequate constraints, process-model mismatch, feedback and multi-controller causal scenarios. | Model/analyst subjectivity, scalability, limited probability/material detail and incomplete comparative validation. | Meaningful control structure and loss/hazard boundary; participants understand real control/operations. | Software, autonomy, human-automation, interface and organisational control constraints/design changes. | Losses/hazards, compact control model, decision-relevant unsafe actions/scenarios and allocated constraints. | FMEA/FMECA, FTA, HAZOP, quantitative analysis, human factors and formal verification. | A simple component failure and deterministic control completely describe the hazard. | S017; S018; S019; S020 |
| Bow-tie / barrier analysis | PROCESS_SAFETY_LINEAGE / CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING | Threat pathways to a top event and consequence pathways, with preventive and mitigative barriers. | May imply static independent barriers, omit control/timing interactions and reduce quality to barrier count. | Top event, threats, consequences and barrier functions are meaningful and monitorable. | Barrier ownership, performance standards, degradation monitoring and emergency planning. | Hazard-specific barriers with function, dependency, owner and health evidence. | FTA/ETA, HAZOP, common-cause, STPA and operational monitoring. | A direct elimination/constraint removes the hazard without layered propagation. | S056; S057; S075; S102 |
| Scenario and causal-path analysis | CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING | Temporal/contextual sequences, alternatives, interactions, escalation, degraded modes and recovery. | Scenario explosion, story bias and unknown unknowns; likelihood may be unclear. | Representative state/context selection and disciplined counterfactual challenge. | Control timing, transition design, tests, containment, emergency and restart criteria. | Only scenarios that test a material constraint, assumption or decision. | FTA/ETA, STPA, HAZOP, FMEA and formal/state-space analysis. | One deterministic state transition proves the claim. | S018; S040; S096 |
| Common-cause/dependent-failure analysis | RELIABILITY_ANCESTRY | Shared design, specification, environment, utilities, maintenance, data and organisational dependencies across nominally redundant controls. | Unknown correlations, software/data commonality and changing suppliers/operations are hard to quantify. | Dependency sources and configurations can be elicited and challenged. | Diversity, segregation, surveillance, architecture simplification and degraded-mode restrictions. | Explicit independence claim with plausible common sources and evidence, not a generic checklist. | FMEA/FTA, defence in depth, assurance provenance and integration testing. | There is one simple control with no redundancy/independence claim. | S050; S056; S087 |
| Human-reliability / human-factors analysis | HUMAN_FACTORS_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY | Task demands, workload, interface/mode, information, timing, staffing, foreseeable use error and recovery. | Human error probabilities can be weakly calibrated; decomposed tasks may omit local rationality and organisation. | Representative users/work, realistic context and non-blaming evidence access. | Interface, automation, staffing, procedures, training and authority redesign. | Observe/represent actual work and connect findings to hazard/control changes. | STPA, HAZOP, scenario analysis, usability testing and organisational analysis. | No consequential human interaction exists or direct physical prevention removes dependence. | S063; S064; S106 |
| Threat/hazard analysis for cyber-physical systems | HYBRID / DOMAIN_TRANSLATION | Malicious and accidental pathways affecting safety-critical control, feedback, availability, data and updates. | Open threat space, secrecy, fast change and inconsistent safety/security semantics. | Shared architecture/configuration view and joint authority. | Segmentation, authentication, safe patching, degraded service, monitoring and incident/recovery design. | Only attack/fault paths with credible safety consequences and coordinated controls. | STPA, FTA, FMEA, change impact, security threat models and operational monitoring. | No plausible adversarial path reaches a safety-relevant function. | S026; S028; S061 |
| Formal methods/model checking | CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING | Precisely specified state, logic, timing and invariant properties within an abstraction. | Specification/model/configuration correspondence; tool assumptions; physical and organisational context omission. | Precise property, valid abstraction and traceable implementation/configuration. | Corner-state elimination, invariant proof, control logic and evidence diversification. | Prove a hazard-linked property whose uncertainty materially affects a decision; validate abstraction. | Testing, simulation, inspection, STPA/FTA and operational evidence. | A direct execution/test conclusively settles a simple reversible property. | S049; S100 |
| Safety/assurance case | SAFETY_ASSURANCE_LINEAGE | Claims, arguments, evidence, assumptions, context, defeaters and acceptance—not hazard discovery by itself. | False premises, omitted hazards, stale/dependent evidence, rhetoric and after-the-fact confirmation. | Live decision consumer, trustworthy evidence, current configuration and challenge authority. | Synthesis, explicit confidence/uncertainty, residual-risk acceptance and change/reuse decisions. | The smallest current argument sufficient for the consequential decision. | All hazard, verification, test and operational evidence methods. | A narrow deterministic claim is settled by direct evidence and ordinary authority. | S042; S043; S044; S045; S046; S048 |


## EVOLVED_SYSTEMS_SAFETY_RISK_AND_UNCERTAINTY_MODEL

- Start with explicit unacceptable loss and hazardous system state; do not let a score define the hazard.
- Keep consequence, exposure, likelihood/frequency/probability, epistemic uncertainty, dependence and assumptions distinguishable.
- For rare catastrophic or systematic interaction hazards, low observed frequency can be weak evidence rather than reassurance.
- Quantitative PRA can support sensitivity and resource decisions when model/data/configuration are credible; it remains model-dependent.
- Ordinal risk matrices can support coarse discussion but cannot be treated as objective arithmetic truth or sufficient acceptance evidence.
- SIL/ASIL/DAL attach graded rigour to safety functions/failure conditions; they are not direct whole-system safety probabilities.
- Residual-risk acceptance is an authority and values decision informed by engineering evidence, not produced by arithmetic alone.
- ALARP/SFAIRP preserves a practicability/proportionality burden but is jurisdiction-specific and not a universal formula.
- Control strength should rise with consequence, irreversibility, coupling, observability latency, recovery difficulty and uncertainty.
- When a direct deterministic constraint settles a local reversible question, extra quantification has no decision value.

### Risk-representation profiles

#### ESS-001 — Explicit unacceptable-loss framing

- **RISK_REPRESENTATION:** Explicit loss/hazard, consequence, uncertainty, exposure, control state and assumptions relevant to Explicit unacceptable-loss framing.
- **WHAT_IT_CAN_JUSTIFY:** Prevents safety effort from becoming method-first and exposes value conflicts early.
- **WHAT_IT_CANNOT_JUSTIFY:** It cannot establish complete hazard knowledge, eliminate uncertainty or substitute a score/label for competent acceptance.
- **UNCERTAINTY_BOUNDARY:** No source establishes one universal loss vocabulary or acceptable threshold.
- **DATA_REQUIREMENTS:** Evidence that the loss set still matches current use, users, environment and public exposure.
- **GAMING_RISK:** Losses framed too broadly become slogans; too narrowly omit public/mission harms; economic inconvenience can be mislabelled as safety.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** For trivial reversible work, state the bounded loss in one line and use the authoritative deterministic check; no elaborate taxonomy.
- **MATURE_FORM:** A concise, current, decision-linked definition of unacceptable loss that bounds later analysis without pretending completeness.


#### ESS-002 — Hazardous system-state framing distinct from failure

- **RISK_REPRESENTATION:** Explicit loss/hazard, consequence, uncertainty, exposure, control state and assumptions relevant to Hazardous system-state framing distinct from failure.
- **WHAT_IT_CAN_JUSTIFY:** Broadens causal coverage and separates what must be prevented from how it may arise.
- **WHAT_IT_CANNOT_JUSTIFY:** It cannot establish complete hazard knowledge, eliminate uncertainty or substitute a score/label for competent acceptance.
- **UNCERTAINTY_BOUNDARY:** No practical method can prove that all hazards have been identified in an open sociotechnical system.
- **DATA_REQUIREMENTS:** Observable indicators of hazardous state, exposure and boundary conditions—not only component health.
- **GAMING_RISK:** Hazards become vague nouns, duplicate losses, or are listed without a consumer/control.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** A simple local task with a complete deterministic invariant may use that invariant directly rather than a separate hazard ontology.
- **MATURE_FORM:** A current loss-linked hazardous-state model with explicit boundary, exposure and causal assumptions.


#### ESS-019 — Uncertainty-aware risk representation rather than score-only governance

- **RISK_REPRESENTATION:** Separate consequence, probability/frequency where defensible, epistemic uncertainty, dependence, exposure and assumptions.
- **WHAT_IT_CAN_JUSTIFY:** Sensitivity-aware comparison, prioritised learning, proportional controls and explicit residual-risk decisions.
- **WHAT_IT_CANNOT_JUSTIFY:** Objective truth from an ordinal cell; precise catastrophic frequency without data/model support; moral acceptability by arithmetic alone.
- **UNCERTAINTY_BOUNDARY:** State data scarcity, model form, dependence and unknown-hazard limits.
- **DATA_REQUIREMENTS:** Traceable event/exposure data, calibrated experts where needed, configuration match and sensitivity analysis.
- **GAMING_RISK:** Category boundaries, likelihood downgrading, severity averaging and selective data windows.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** Use a direct deterministic constraint or qualitative consequence/uncertainty statement where it already decides.
- **MATURE_FORM:** Decision-linked plural risk representation with explicit uncertainty and no score-as-truth.


#### ESS-020 — Consequence, reversibility, coupling and observability proportionality

- **RISK_REPRESENTATION:** Explicit loss/hazard, consequence, uncertainty, exposure, control state and assumptions relevant to Consequence, reversibility, coupling and observability proportionality.
- **WHAT_IT_CAN_JUSTIFY:** Concentrates scarce safety effort where it has expected decision value and preserves speed where risk is bounded.
- **WHAT_IT_CANNOT_JUSTIFY:** It cannot establish complete hazard knowledge, eliminate uncertainty or substitute a score/label for competent acceptance.
- **UNCERTAINTY_BOUNDARY:** No universal scalar combines consequence, reversibility, coupling and observability without information loss.
- **DATA_REQUIREMENTS:** Actual propagation/recovery performance, false-stop cost, near misses and whether controls change decisions.
- **GAMING_RISK:** Risk-class gaming, simplistic matrices, certification-category lock-in and underestimating systemic coupling.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** Local, cheap, reversible, immediately observable work with an authoritative discriminator uses a minimal check and normal engineering review.
- **MATURE_FORM:** Control strength rises with credible loss and irreversibility/coupling/latency, while deterministic low-risk work remains cheap.


#### ESS-021 — Explicit residual-risk acceptance by competent authority

- **RISK_REPRESENTATION:** Named residual hazards, consequence, uncertainty, exposure, control status, assumptions and validity period.
- **WHAT_IT_CAN_JUSTIFY:** A bounded decision to operate, test, defer or add controls under explicit authority.
- **WHAT_IT_CANNOT_JUSTIFY:** Erasing moral/legal duties, accepting an unknown hazard, or converting weak evidence into safety.
- **UNCERTAINTY_BOUNDARY:** Unknown mechanisms, sparse data and changing exposure remain visible and can trigger precaution or monitoring.
- **DATA_REQUIREMENTS:** Current hazard/control evidence, practicable alternatives, exposed populations and change-sensitive assumptions.
- **GAMING_RISK:** Likelihood downgrading, fragmented hazards, acceptance at too-low authority and indefinite waivers.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** Ordinary delegated decision when consequence is trivial, reversible and deterministically bounded.
- **MATURE_FORM:** Competent, explicit, time/configuration-bounded residual-risk acceptance with reopening triggers.


#### ESS-022 — Proportionate risk reduction under ALARP or SFAIRP reasoning

- **RISK_REPRESENTATION:** Explicit loss/hazard, consequence, uncertainty, exposure, control state and assumptions relevant to Proportionate risk reduction under ALARP or SFAIRP reasoning.
- **WHAT_IT_CAN_JUSTIFY:** Forces search beyond threshold compliance while retaining proportionality and practical feasibility.
- **WHAT_IT_CANNOT_JUSTIFY:** It cannot establish complete hazard knowledge, eliminate uncertainty or substitute a score/label for competent acceptance.
- **UNCERTAINTY_BOUNDARY:** No strong comparative evidence establishes ALARP as the optimal decision rule across cultures, rights regimes or catastrophic uncertainty.
- **DATA_REQUIREMENTS:** Control effectiveness, changing good practice, exposure, sacrifice estimates and evidence that adopted controls remain operative.
- **GAMING_RISK:** Back-calculated numbers, monetisation controversy, threshold gaming and invoking cost before identifying controls.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** Where a binding deterministic rule or clearly trivial reversible hazard settles the decision, use it directly rather than manufacture a cost-benefit case.
- **MATURE_FORM:** Use proportionality as disciplined justification for control sufficiency, not as a numerical escape hatch or universal legal export.


#### ESS-024 — Safety-integrity and development-assurance rigour tied to safety functions

- **RISK_REPRESENTATION:** Explicit loss/hazard, consequence, uncertainty, exposure, control state and assumptions relevant to Safety-integrity and development-assurance rigour tied to safety functions.
- **WHAT_IT_CAN_JUSTIFY:** Concentrates disciplined architecture and verification on functions whose loss could be consequential.
- **WHAT_IT_CANNOT_JUSTIFY:** It cannot establish complete hazard knowledge, eliminate uncertainty or substitute a score/label for competent acceptance.
- **UNCERTAINTY_BOUNDARY:** Exact process prescriptions and claimed probability correspondences have limited independent outcome validation.
- **DATA_REQUIREMENTS:** Function demand/success, diagnostic coverage, systematic-defect controls, requirement/verification coverage and configuration identity.
- **GAMING_RISK:** Level inflation, lowest-bid evidence production, rote objective completion and scope gaps such as intended-function hazards.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** Do not assign a high assurance level to low-consequence code or use the classification where a direct deterministic test fully settles a local reversible change.
- **MATURE_FORM:** Use graded integrity objectives as one hazard-derived assurance mechanism, never as a numerical certificate of total system safety.


#### ESS-038 — Bounded emergency or temporary risk acceptance with compensating controls

- **RISK_REPRESENTATION:** Explicit loss/hazard, consequence, uncertainty, exposure, control state and assumptions relevant to Bounded emergency or temporary risk acceptance with compensating controls.
- **WHAT_IT_CAN_JUSTIFY:** Allows necessary bounded operation without hiding the increased risk or normalising impairment.
- **WHAT_IT_CANNOT_JUSTIFY:** It cannot establish complete hazard knowledge, eliminate uncertainty or substitute a score/label for competent acceptance.
- **UNCERTAINTY_BOUNDARY:** Comparative evidence on waiver governance is limited and emergency decisions may remain ethically contested.
- **DATA_REQUIREMENTS:** Time/exposure, compensating-control health, changed conditions, incidents, handoffs and restoration progress.
- **GAMING_RISK:** Waiver culture, deadline renewal, paper compensations, authority diffusion and production pressure redefining emergencies.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** Do not create a waiver for trivial work already inside ordinary authority, and do not use temporary acceptance to avoid feasible permanent correction.
- **MATURE_FORM:** Exceptional operation is safe enough only within an observable, time/configuration-bounded envelope whose compensating controls and authority remain current.


#### ESS-050 — Safety margins, operating envelopes and boundary separation

- **RISK_REPRESENTATION:** Explicit loss/hazard, consequence, uncertainty, exposure, control state and assumptions relevant to Safety margins, operating envelopes and boundary separation.
- **WHAT_IT_CAN_JUSTIFY:** Provides time and robustness against uncertainty rather than relying on perfect threshold prediction.
- **WHAT_IT_CANNOT_JUSTIFY:** It cannot establish complete hazard knowledge, eliminate uncertainty or substitute a score/label for competent acceptance.
- **UNCERTAINTY_BOUNDARY:** Complex interactions may create moving or unknown boundaries, and excessive margins can create mission/availability harms.
- **DATA_REQUIREMENTS:** Distance to limit, uncertainty, rate of approach, ageing/degradation, excursions, recovery time and barrier availability.
- **GAMING_RISK:** Arbitrary factors, margin hoarding, false precision, hidden multidimensional boundaries and workarounds around over-conservative limits.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** For a low-consequence reversible state with immediate deterministic feedback, ordinary tolerance checks may suffice.
- **MATURE_FORM:** Maintain enough observable separation from hazardous boundaries to absorb credible uncertainty and response latency, while revising limits when evidence changes.


#### ESS-055 — Risk-matrix cell treated as objective risk or sufficient decision evidence

- **RISK_REPRESENTATION:** Ordinal severity/likelihood cell.
- **WHAT_IT_CAN_JUSTIFY:** At most transparent coarse discussion or triage under explicit limitations.
- **WHAT_IT_CANNOT_JUSTIFY:** Objective risk, valid arithmetic ranking, precise probability, acceptable residual risk or control sufficiency.
- **UNCERTAINTY_BOUNDARY:** Usually hidden or compressed; this is a principal defect.
- **DATA_REQUIREMENTS:** Even good category data do not cure ordinal/range problems.
- **GAMING_RISK:** Very high at thresholds, likelihood labels and severity aggregation.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** State consequence and uncertainty directly or apply a deterministic constraint.
- **MATURE_FORM:** Do not treat a matrix score as truth; use decision-linked consequence and uncertainty reasoning.


#### ESS-058 — Zero observed incidents treated as proof that controls work

- **RISK_REPRESENTATION:** Explicit loss/hazard, consequence, uncertainty, exposure, control state and assumptions relevant to Zero observed incidents treated as proof that controls work.
- **WHAT_IT_CAN_JUSTIFY:** No general proof payoff; outcome data are one evidence stream.
- **WHAT_IT_CANNOT_JUSTIFY:** It cannot establish complete hazard knowledge, eliminate uncertainty or substitute a score/label for competent acceptance.
- **UNCERTAINTY_BOUNDARY:** Long exposure without incidents can update probability under a valid stable model, but rarely proves control efficacy by itself.
- **DATA_REQUIREMENTS:** Exposure-adjusted events, near misses, reporting quality, barrier demand/success and precursor trends.
- **GAMING_RISK:** Incentive to suppress reports, celebratory complacency, regression to the mean and delayed detection of latent risk.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** Use direct inspections/tests/control-state measures or an authoritative deterministic discriminator where available.
- **MATURE_FORM:** NO_GENERAL_PROPERTY in incident-free proof; require evidence proportionate to rarity, exposure and causal control state.


#### ESS-064 — Zero-risk or absolute-safety requirement as a general engineering target

- **RISK_REPRESENTATION:** Explicit loss/hazard, consequence, uncertainty, exposure, control state and assumptions relevant to Zero-risk or absolute-safety requirement as a general engineering target.
- **WHAT_IT_CAN_JUSTIFY:** No general payoff as an absolute target; specific loss constraints and ALARP/proportional control are retained.
- **WHAT_IT_CANNOT_JUSTIFY:** It cannot establish complete hazard knowledge, eliminate uncertainty or substitute a score/label for competent acceptance.
- **UNCERTAINTY_BOUNDARY:** Some domains legitimately prohibit particular single failures or exposures; rejection is of universal absolute risk elimination.
- **DATA_REQUIREMENTS:** Residual hazards, uncertainty, exposure, alternatives, operational evidence and competing service harms.
- **GAMING_RISK:** Paralysis, risk transfer, dishonest “zero” certification, excessive false stops and suppression of uncertainty.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** Use deterministic prohibitions for specific unacceptable states, not a universal claim that all risk is zero.
- **MATURE_FORM:** NO_GENERAL_PROPERTY in absolute safety; engineer against specified unacceptable losses with bounded evidence and transparent residual uncertainty.


## EVOLVED_SYSTEMS_SAFETY_ASSURANCE_AND_EVIDENCE_MODEL

Assurance is a **defeasible, configuration-bound decision argument**. Its unit is not document volume but the relevance, validity, independence, currentness and challenge of evidence for a bounded claim.

| FALSE EQUIVALENCE | REQUIRED DISTINCTION | WHY |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claim documented | Claim justified | Documentation is a representation; justification requires relevant valid current evidence and sound reasoning. |
| Many evidence items | Independent evidence | Items can share requirements, models, tools, oracles, data and incentives. |
| Case internally coherent | System safe | Coherence does not establish premise truth, hazard completeness or configuration correspondence. |
| Certification accepted | Operational risk eliminated | Acceptance is bounded by scope, configuration, assumptions and continuing operation/change. |
| Historical evidence valid | Current configuration covered | Reuse requires identity/equivalence and unchanged assumptions/control paths. |
| Reviewer organisationally independent | Evidence informationally independent | Separate organisations can reproduce one common error or source. |
| Requirement satisfied | Unsafe interaction impossible | Locally satisfied requirements can conflict or omit context/timing/composition. |
| Traceability link present | Semantic causal closure | Links can all derive from a flawed premise or stale configuration. |
| Proof complete | Physical system claim true | Proof is conditional on specification, abstraction, tool and implementation mapping. |
| Dashboard green | Assumptions and controls current | Telemetry can be circular, delayed, gameable or blind to unknown hazards. |


### Safety-assurance profiles

#### ESS-018 — Traceability from hazards and constraints to implementation and verification

- **PROPERTY:** Traceability from hazards and constraints to implementation and verification
- **CLAIM:** The bounded safety proposition addressed by Traceability from hazards and constraints to implementation and verification is justified for the identified configuration and decision.
- **ARGUMENT:** Maintain bidirectional, configuration-bound links and test whether every claim has a control and every control has a hazard rationale.
- **EVIDENCE:** Current configuration, verification result, unresolved links, waivers and operational monitoring.
- **ASSUMPTIONS_AND_CONTEXT:** Stable identifiers, configuration management and semantic—not merely hyperlink—traceability.
- **DEFEATERS_OR_CHALLENGES:** Traceability is not proof; linked requirements can all be wrong or derived from one flawed assumption.
- **INDEPENDENCE_REQUIREMENT:** Scale independent challenge and evidence diversity to consequence, uncertainty and common-source risk.
- **CURRENTNESS_OR_CHANGE_TRIGGER:** Consequential controls, regulated development and systems with many suppliers/changes. Reopen whenever configuration, assumptions, evidence validity or exposure changes materially.
- **DECISION_OR_CONSUMER:** Design authority, verifier, assurance case owner and change authority.
- **FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED:** Trace-link volume without semantic review, auto-generated false completeness and unmaintainable matrices.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** For a tiny local deterministic change, one direct link from hazard/invariant to test result may be sufficient.
- **MATURE_FORM:** Maintain only decision-relevant traceability sufficient to show current hazard-to-control-to-evidence closure.


#### ESS-024 — Safety-integrity and development-assurance rigour tied to safety functions

- **PROPERTY:** Safety-integrity and development-assurance rigour tied to safety functions
- **CLAIM:** The bounded safety proposition addressed by Safety-integrity and development-assurance rigour tied to safety functions is justified for the identified configuration and decision.
- **ARGUMENT:** Derive integrity/assurance needs from hazards and functions; meet domain architecture and process objectives; verify actual function and complement with interaction analysis.
- **EVIDENCE:** Function demand/success, diagnostic coverage, systematic-defect controls, requirement/verification coverage and configuration identity.
- **ASSUMPTIONS_AND_CONTEXT:** Valid hazard classification, allocated safety function, domain applicability and evidence that architecture and verification objectives are met.
- **DEFEATERS_OR_CHALLENGES:** Standards authority is strong but comparative evidence for exact level/process prescriptions is limited; SOTIF exists because malfunction-only scope is incomplete.
- **INDEPENDENCE_REQUIREMENT:** Scale independent challenge and evidence diversity to consequence, uncertainty and common-source risk.
- **CURRENTNESS_OR_CHANGE_TRIGGER:** Safety-related E/E/PE, airborne software/hardware and automotive functions whose failure conditions justify graded assurance. Reopen whenever configuration, assumptions, evidence validity or exposure changes materially.
- **DECISION_OR_CONSUMER:** System safety assessor, functional-safety manager, certification authority and integrator.
- **FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED:** Level inflation, lowest-bid evidence production, rote objective completion and scope gaps such as intended-function hazards.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** Do not assign a high assurance level to low-consequence code or use the classification where a direct deterministic test fully settles a local reversible change.
- **MATURE_FORM:** Use graded integrity objectives as one hazard-derived assurance mechanism, never as a numerical certificate of total system safety.


#### ESS-025 — Informational independence and diversity of assurance evidence

- **PROPERTY:** Informational independence and diversity of assurance evidence
- **CLAIM:** The consequential safety claim is supported by evidence with sufficiently distinct failure modes.
- **ARGUMENT:** Show how each evidence item bears on the claim and disclose common premises, data, tools and oracles.
- **EVIDENCE:** Diverse analysis, formal proof where applicable, testing, operational data and authorised independent challenge.
- **ASSUMPTIONS_AND_CONTEXT:** Current configuration, common-source map, tool qualification and competence/incentive conditions.
- **DEFEATERS_OR_CHALLENGES:** Shared requirements, correlated teams, common test oracle, copied artefacts and unavailable negative evidence.
- **INDEPENDENCE_REQUIREMENT:** Informational, methodological and incentive independence proportional to consequence; organisational separation alone is insufficient.
- **CURRENTNESS_OR_CHANGE_TRIGGER:** Reassess when source, model, tool, supplier, configuration or operational context changes.
- **DECISION_OR_CONSUMER:** Risk acceptor and design/certification authority.
- **FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED:** Excessive separation delays defect feedback and duplicates low-value work.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** One decisive direct check for trivial reversible claims.
- **MATURE_FORM:** A provenance-aware portfolio of independently informative evidence.


#### ESS-026 — Claim–argument–evidence safety assurance

- **PROPERTY:** Claim–argument–evidence safety assurance
- **CLAIM:** A bounded safety proposition needed for a live decision.
- **ARGUMENT:** Explicit reasoning connecting evidence to the claim under stated context and assumptions.
- **EVIDENCE:** Hazard analyses, design artefacts, tests, analyses, inspections and current operational evidence.
- **ASSUMPTIONS_AND_CONTEXT:** System boundary, configuration, environment, validity period and delegated authorities.
- **DEFEATERS_OR_CHALLENGES:** Counterexamples, missing scenarios, invalid tools/data, dependence, uncertainty and operational anomalies.
- **INDEPENDENCE_REQUIREMENT:** Challenge and evidence diversity scale with consequence.
- **CURRENTNESS_OR_CHANGE_TRIGGER:** Any change to claim, configuration, assumptions, environment or evidence validity.
- **DECISION_OR_CONSUMER:** Named design, operational, certification or risk-acceptance decision.
- **FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED:** A case can become a large after-the-fact compliance narrative with no engineering consumer.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** A compact rationale linked to one decisive check for a narrow reversible claim.
- **MATURE_FORM:** Living, challengeable, configuration-bound assurance used to make and revisit decisions.


#### ESS-027 — Defeaters, counterevidence and authorised challenge in assurance

- **PROPERTY:** Defeaters, counterevidence and authorised challenge in assurance
- **CLAIM:** The bounded safety proposition addressed by Defeaters, counterevidence and authorised challenge in assurance is justified for the identified configuration and decision.
- **ARGUMENT:** Record defeaters and contrary evidence, empower technically competent challenge, assign closure criteria and preserve unresolved uncertainty in acceptance.
- **EVIDENCE:** Open objections, negative tests, anomaly trends, premise failures, response quality and whether decisions changed.
- **ASSUMPTIONS_AND_CONTEXT:** Psychological/organisational safety for dissent, traceable challenge state and a decision process that can change course.
- **DEFEATERS_OR_CHALLENGES:** Challenge quality is difficult to measure; more reviewers can repeat the same assumptions or paralyse decisions.
- **INDEPENDENCE_REQUIREMENT:** Scale independent challenge and evidence diversity to consequence, uncertainty and common-source risk.
- **CURRENTNESS_OR_CHANGE_TRIGGER:** High-consequence or model-sensitive claims, novel systems and changes that invalidate prior assumptions. Reopen whenever configuration, assumptions, evidence validity or exposure changes materially.
- **DECISION_OR_CONSUMER:** Independent assessor, workforce/operator, safety board and accountable decision owner.
- **FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED:** Performative red teaming, endless objections without decision criteria, retaliation and burying challenges in appendices.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** For a settled low-consequence deterministic claim, one sanity check is enough; adversarial boards add no value.
- **MATURE_FORM:** A consequential claim remains provisional until material defeaters are eliminated, controlled, or explicitly accepted by the right authority.


#### ESS-028 — Configuration identity binding for safety evidence

- **PROPERTY:** Configuration identity binding for safety evidence
- **CLAIM:** The bounded safety proposition addressed by Configuration identity binding for safety evidence is justified for the identified configuration and decision.
- **ARGUMENT:** Record decision-relevant configuration identifiers and evidence provenance; verify deployed identity and invalidate/reassess affected claims on divergence.
- **EVIDENCE:** Build/component IDs, calibration, parameters, environment, evidence version, deployment inventory and deviations.
- **ASSUMPTIONS_AND_CONTEXT:** Controlled baselines, deployment observability, supplier/change notification and an impact model.
- **DEFEATERS_OR_CHALLENGES:** A hash or baseline name does not prove behavioural equivalence; operational environment and hidden dependencies may still differ.
- **INDEPENDENCE_REQUIREMENT:** Scale independent challenge and evidence diversity to consequence, uncertainty and common-source risk.
- **CURRENTNESS_OR_CHANGE_TRIGGER:** Any safety-relevant change, distributed deployment, supplier substitution or long-lived assurance claim. Reopen whenever configuration, assumptions, evidence validity or exposure changes materially.
- **DECISION_OR_CONSUMER:** Configuration manager, release authority, safety case owner, operator and assessor.
- **FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED:** Identifier bureaucracy without semantic impact, uncontrolled runtime adaptation and false confidence in nominal version labels.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** For a local disposable reversible experiment, identify only the artefact and conditions necessary to reproduce the decisive check.
- **MATURE_FORM:** No consequential safety claim is reusable without demonstrating that its configuration, environment and assumptions still match.


#### ESS-029 — Safety impact analysis and proportionate re-assurance after change

- **PROPERTY:** Safety impact analysis and proportionate re-assurance after change
- **CLAIM:** The bounded safety proposition addressed by Safety impact analysis and proportionate re-assurance after change is justified for the identified configuration and decision.
- **ARGUMENT:** Use traceable impact analysis from change to hazards, interactions, constraints and evidence; test the affected frontier and monitor uncertain effects.
- **EVIDENCE:** Diff/configuration identity, changed assumptions, affected tests, operational telemetry, regression and rollback readiness.
- **ASSUMPTIONS_AND_CONTEXT:** Current baseline, dependency/interface model, hazard state and authority to classify/escalate change.
- **DEFEATERS_OR_CHALLENGES:** Incremental assurance depends on accurate impact models; complex adaptive interactions can defeat locality assumptions.
- **INDEPENDENCE_REQUIREMENT:** Scale independent challenge and evidence diversity to consequence, uncertainty and common-source risk.
- **CURRENTNESS_OR_CHANGE_TRIGGER:** Software, hardware, supplier, environment, procedure, security and organisational changes with plausible hazard reach. Reopen whenever configuration, assumptions, evidence validity or exposure changes materially.
- **DECISION_OR_CONSUMER:** Change control, release authority, system safety, operator and regulator/certifier.
- **FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED:** Form-based classification, hidden cumulative change, reusing stale evidence, certification avoidance and blanket rework.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** A trivial local reversible change with a decisive regression discriminator uses that check and records only the necessary identity.
- **MATURE_FORM:** Re-establish exactly the safety claims whose system, assumptions, controls or evidence may have changed; justify both reuse and new work.


#### ESS-030 — Living, current and operationally connected assurance

- **PROPERTY:** Living, current and operationally connected assurance
- **CLAIM:** The bounded safety proposition addressed by Living, current and operationally connected assurance is justified for the identified configuration and decision.
- **ARGUMENT:** Define change and operational triggers, connect leading evidence to claims, reassess affected arguments and require decision closure.
- **EVIDENCE:** Configuration, control health, incidents/precursors, assumption monitors, evidence expiry and operational-envelope excursions.
- **ASSUMPTIONS_AND_CONTEXT:** Stable claim architecture, configuration identity, trusted telemetry, trigger thresholds and resourced decision owners.
- **DEFEATERS_OR_CHALLENGES:** Continuous assurance cannot observe unknown hazards and may privilege measurable proxies over causal control state.
- **INDEPENDENCE_REQUIREMENT:** Scale independent challenge and evidence diversity to consequence, uncertainty and common-source risk.
- **CURRENTNESS_OR_CHANGE_TRIGGER:** Long-lived software-intensive, autonomous, security-exposed or operationally adapting systems. Reopen whenever configuration, assumptions, evidence validity or exposure changes materially.
- **DECISION_OR_CONSUMER:** Operator, safety case owner, release authority, regulator and maintenance organisation.
- **FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED:** Dashboard theatre, noisy triggers, automated circular evidence, alert fatigue and impossible real-time completeness.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** Static assurance can suffice for a stable, bounded, short-lived and readily observed system; update only when a relevant trigger occurs.
- **MATURE_FORM:** Assurance remains valid only while named configuration, assumptions, controls and evidence are current; relevant changes trigger bounded reassessment.


#### ESS-031 — Independent assessment and IV&V where consequence warrants

- **PROPERTY:** Independent assessment and IV&V where consequence warrants
- **CLAIM:** The bounded safety proposition addressed by Independent assessment and IV&V where consequence warrants is justified for the identified configuration and decision.
- **ARGUMENT:** Define risk-based scope, give assessors evidence/tool/access rights, seek independent information and close material findings before acceptance.
- **EVIDENCE:** Independent defect findings, evidence provenance, unresolved dissent, retest results and configuration coverage.
- **ASSUMPTIONS_AND_CONTEXT:** Competence, access, independence, clear claim scope and response authority.
- **DEFEATERS_OR_CHALLENGES:** Controlled multiversion evidence and assurance failures show that nominal independence can remain correlated.
- **INDEPENDENCE_REQUIREMENT:** Scale independent challenge and evidence diversity to consequence, uncertainty and common-source risk.
- **CURRENTNESS_OR_CHANGE_TRIGGER:** Catastrophic or irreversible failure conditions, novel technology, weak testability, conflicted suppliers or mandated domains. Reopen whenever configuration, assumptions, evidence validity or exposure changes materially.
- **DECISION_OR_CONSUMER:** Risk acceptor, certification authority, programme executive and operator.
- **FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED:** Expensive late paperwork, adversarial handoff, duplicated evidence and false inference that separation guarantees independence.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** Routine peer review or one deterministic check is sufficient for low-consequence reversible work; separate IV&V should not trigger by label alone.
- **MATURE_FORM:** Deploy independent assessment only where its distinct information and challenge authority justify cost, and measure it by decisions/findings rather than signatures.


#### ESS-032 — Evidence triangulation and targeted formal verification

- **PROPERTY:** Evidence triangulation and targeted formal verification
- **CLAIM:** The bounded safety proposition addressed by Evidence triangulation and targeted formal verification is justified for the identified configuration and decision.
- **ARGUMENT:** For each consequential claim, select the least set of analyses/tests/inspections/operational evidence that attacks distinct failure modes; prove only tractable decisive properties.
- **EVIDENCE:** Proof obligations, model assumptions, code/configuration correspondence, test coverage and operational anomalies.
- **ASSUMPTIONS_AND_CONTEXT:** Precise property and model, validated abstraction, configuration mapping, trustworthy tools and a decision consumer.
- **DEFEATERS_OR_CHALLENGES:** Formal proof establishes only the modelled property under assumptions; outcome superiority over disciplined testing is context dependent.
- **INDEPENDENCE_REQUIREMENT:** Scale independent challenge and evidence diversity to consequence, uncertainty and common-source risk.
- **CURRENTNESS_OR_CHANGE_TRIGGER:** Complex logic, concurrency, control laws, protection functions or rare combinations where exhaustive empirical testing is infeasible. Reopen whenever configuration, assumptions, evidence validity or exposure changes materially.
- **DECISION_OR_CONSUMER:** Designer, verifier, safety case owner and independent assessor.
- **FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED:** Proof theatre, unverifiable models, tool-chain dependence, duplicated evidence and formal work disconnected from hazard decisions.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** Use direct execution, inspection or deterministic testing when it fully settles a simple claim; formalisation must earn its cost.
- **MATURE_FORM:** Use formal methods selectively where a precise hazard-linked property and abstraction make them decisively informative, then triangulate model correspondence.


#### ESS-044 — Supplier and contractor boundary assurance with change notification

- **PROPERTY:** Supplier and contractor boundary assurance with change notification
- **CLAIM:** The bounded safety proposition addressed by Supplier and contractor boundary assurance with change notification is justified for the identified configuration and decision.
- **ARGUMENT:** Allocate hazard-linked obligations and interface assumptions, require evidence and change/anomaly notification, verify integration and retain integrator accountability.
- **EVIDENCE:** Supplier versions, deviations, anomalies, process/evidence changes, interface conformance and field performance.
- **ASSUMPTIONS_AND_CONTEXT:** Clear technical/contract boundary, component criticality, integration testability, configuration provenance and enforceable notification terms.
- **DEFEATERS_OR_CHALLENGES:** Contracts cannot reveal unknown interactions or guarantee candour; excessive requirements can reduce supplier diversity and agility.
- **INDEPENDENCE_REQUIREMENT:** Scale independent challenge and evidence diversity to consequence, uncertainty and common-source risk.
- **CURRENTNESS_OR_CHANGE_TRIGGER:** Safety-relevant purchased software/hardware, outsourced operations/maintenance and multi-tier supply chains. Reopen whenever configuration, assumptions, evidence validity or exposure changes materially.
- **DECISION_OR_CONSUMER:** Integrator, supplier quality/safety, procurement, configuration/change authority and operator.
- **FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED:** Flow-down paperwork, supplier scorecards, proprietary evidence dead ends, duplicated audits and false transfer of responsibility.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** Commodity low-consequence components with a decisive acceptance test can use that test rather than imposing a full supplier safety system.
- **MATURE_FORM:** Match supplier assurance to system consequence and interface uncertainty, but keep the integrator responsible for composed safety.


#### ESS-048 — Live decision consumer for every safety artefact and control

- **PROPERTY:** Live decision consumer for every safety artefact and control
- **CLAIM:** The bounded safety proposition addressed by Live decision consumer for every safety artefact and control is justified for the identified configuration and decision.
- **ARGUMENT:** State the decision, consumer, trigger and required information before producing the artefact; observe use and retire or redesign if it does not change action.
- **EVIDENCE:** Decision made, challenge raised, action/acceptance changed, use frequency, stale age and unresolved consumer feedback.
- **ASSUMPTIONS_AND_CONTEXT:** Real decision need, current evidence, accessible representation and consumer authority.
- **DEFEATERS_OR_CHALLENGES:** Some assurance artefacts serve latent legal/public accountability and rare future decisions, so immediate use alone is not sufficient.
- **INDEPENDENCE_REQUIREMENT:** Scale independent challenge and evidence diversity to consequence, uncertainty and common-source risk.
- **CURRENTNESS_OR_CHANGE_TRIGGER:** Any recurring safety analysis, review, metric, report, case or control. Reopen whenever configuration, assumptions, evidence validity or exposure changes materially.
- **DECISION_OR_CONSUMER:** Designer, operator, risk acceptor, reviewer/investigator and regulator.
- **FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED:** Artificially naming a consumer, rubber-stamp use, hidden secondary consumers and deleting records needed for future learning.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** Do not create a separate artefact when the decisive information is already embedded in an authoritative engineering/operational control.
- **MATURE_FORM:** Every artefact must earn existence through a current or credibly latent consequential decision and an owner who can act on it.


#### ESS-051 — Explicit assumption validity and monitoring

- **PROPERTY:** Explicit assumption validity and monitoring
- **CLAIM:** The bounded safety proposition addressed by Explicit assumption validity and monitoring is justified for the identified configuration and decision.
- **ARGUMENT:** Identify claim-critical assumptions, assign evidence/owner/validity period, monitor observable ones and trigger restriction or reassessment on violation.
- **EVIDENCE:** Premise status, environmental range, interface/provider behaviour, data drift, independence evidence and violations.
- **ASSUMPTIONS_AND_CONTEXT:** Claim/hazard model, observable discriminators or periodic revalidation, configuration linkage and action authority.
- **DEFEATERS_OR_CHALLENGES:** Unknown unknowns remain outside the register and monitoring can be circular or lagging.
- **INDEPENDENCE_REQUIREMENT:** Scale independent challenge and evidence diversity to consequence, uncertainty and common-source risk.
- **CURRENTNESS_OR_CHANGE_TRIGGER:** Novel, changing, autonomous, outsourced or environment-sensitive systems and any reused safety evidence. Reopen whenever configuration, assumptions, evidence validity or exposure changes materially.
- **DECISION_OR_CONSUMER:** Safety case owner, system architect, operations, supplier and change authority.
- **FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED:** Assumption-log bloat, tautologies, unmonitorable claims, green dashboards from correlated telemetry and no response to violation.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** Do not create a register for obvious transient facts already enforced by a deterministic check; record only assumptions whose failure changes a decision.
- **MATURE_FORM:** A safety claim is valid only while its material assumptions are evidenced; monitor the few premises whose failure can change control or acceptance.


#### ESS-052 — Durable current hazard, constraint and decision state

- **PROPERTY:** Durable current hazard, constraint and decision state
- **CLAIM:** The bounded safety proposition addressed by Durable current hazard, constraint and decision state is justified for the identified configuration and decision.
- **ARGUMENT:** Maintain the minimum durable state needed to understand current hazard/control/acceptance closure; update through change and retire obsolete entries explicitly.
- **EVIDENCE:** Control/evidence status, owner/acceptance, configuration, open scenarios, incidents, changes and review/expiry dates.
- **ASSUMPTIONS_AND_CONTEXT:** Clear semantics, ownership, configuration identity, change triggers and a live decision consumer.
- **DEFEATERS_OR_CHALLENGES:** No log establishes hazard completeness or control effectiveness; it can become a powerful compliance theatre.
- **INDEPENDENCE_REQUIREMENT:** Scale independent challenge and evidence diversity to consequence, uncertainty and common-source risk.
- **CURRENTNESS_OR_CHANGE_TRIGGER:** Long-lived, multi-team or regulated systems and hazards requiring multiple controls/decisions over time. Reopen whenever configuration, assumptions, evidence validity or exposure changes materially.
- **DECISION_OR_CONSUMER:** System safety, design/change authority, operator, assessor and risk acceptor.
- **FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED:** Hazard-log bureaucracy, entry count as quality, stale closure, generic hazards, duplicate analysis and detached spreadsheets.
- **CHEAP_PATH:** A local ephemeral hazard fully eliminated and verified can be recorded in the ordinary work item; a dedicated log is unnecessary.
- **MATURE_FORM:** Preserve current decision-relevant hazard/control memory in any implementation that exposes ownership, evidence, assumptions, change and residual acceptance.


## EVOLVED_SYSTEMS_SAFETY_CHANGE_AND_CONFIGURATION_MODEL

The model rejects both unchecked evidence reuse and universal full re-certification. The question is: **which hazards, constraints, assumptions, interfaces, controls, evidence and authorities may have changed, and what must be re-established?**

| CHANGE CONDITION | MATURE RE-ASSURANCE RESPONSE | PRIMARY FAILURE RISK |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No relevant change and demonstrated configuration/environment equivalence | Reuse prior evidence; verify identity and expiry only. | Configuration mismatch or hidden supplier/runtime drift. |
| Direct change to a safety constraint, control, interface or requirement | Reanalyse affected hazards/scenarios, reverify control and update assurance/acceptance. | File-count or label understates causal reach. |
