| Change to assumption, environment, exposure or use | Revalidate premise and downstream claims; add operational monitoring where uncertainty remains. | Evidence can be technically unchanged but semantically stale. |
| Supplier/component/tool/data change | Assess provenance, equivalence, common cause and integration; require notification/evidence. | Certificate/version label may not establish behaviour. |
| Security patch or urgent emergency change | Use bounded emergency authority, compensating controls, rollback, impact frontier and post-change monitoring. | Urgency suppresses safety regression or delay leaves exploit risk. |
| Low-consequence local reversible change with decisive discriminator | Run direct check, preserve minimal identity/result and escalate only on assumption/scope failure. | Cheap path is misused to hide coupling or irreversible consequence. |
| Cumulative series of individually minor changes | Assess aggregate drift, shared interfaces and assumption erosion; periodically refresh system-level scenarios. | Differential analyses miss emergent composition. |
| Adaptive/online change inside approved envelope | Monitor envelope/assumptions and maintain fallback; changes outside envelope trigger re-assurance. | Runtime telemetry is circular or adaptation escapes authority. |


Minimum change closure:

```text
identify actual baseline and deployed configuration
classify credible consequence and reversibility
trace change to hazards, interfaces, assumptions, controls and evidence
justify unaffected evidence reuse
re-establish affected constraints and end-to-end control
prepare rollback/containment and monitor uncertain effects
update residual-risk decision and hazard/assurance state
```

## EVOLVED_SYSTEMS_SAFETY_CONTAINMENT_RECOVERY_AND_RESTART_MODEL

| STAGE | ENGINEERING PROPERTY | FAILURE TO AVOID | PROPERTY LINK |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Detection | Recognise hazard/degradation with enough time and discrimination for action. | Alarm exists but is late, stale, false or has no consumer. | ESS-034 |
| Containment / isolation | Interrupt propagation and bound energy, material, motion, command or exposure. | Stop command issued but physical/system state is unconfirmed. | ESS-035 |
| Degraded operation | Continue only within a bounded lower-capability envelope when stopping is more dangerous. | Mode confusion, hidden degradation or indefinite temporary operation. | ESS-036 |
| Recovery / rollback | Restore a known compatible configuration and relevant controls. | Rollback reintroduces vulnerability or fails to repair causal mechanism. | ESS-037 |
| Restart authorisation | Confirm restored constraints, feedback, barriers and residual-risk decision before service return. | Service available is mistaken for safe state. | ESS-037 |
| Post-event learning | Investigate causal mechanisms, implement controls and verify effectiveness/recurrence. | Incident closed on report or recommendation issuance. | ESS-039–041 |


```text
hazard detected != hazard contained
shutdown requested != safe state reached
safe state reached != recovery authorised
service restored != safety constraints restored
incident closed != causal mechanism controlled
```

A universal “fail safe” rule is rejected. The mature question is which response—stop, isolate, continue, degrade or recover—minimises credible loss in the current mode, and what feedback proves that the intended state was achieved.

## EVOLVED_SYSTEMS_SAFETY_HUMAN_ORGANISATIONAL_MODEL

| ELEMENT | MATURE PROPERTY | BOUNDARY / FAILURE MODE | SOURCES |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Human action | Treat action as context-dependent control, not self-explanatory error. | Interface, workload, goals, feedback, timing, authority and recovery opportunity. | S063; S064; S106 |
| Local rationality | Reconstruct what information and tradeoffs made action reasonable at the time. | Avoid hindsight while still evaluating competence/duty. | S064 |
| Automation coordination | Analyse mode, process-model mismatch, handoff, override, timing and shared control. | Locally correct human and automation actions can conflict. | S018; S088; S089 |
| Production pressure | Map resource/schedule/metric control paths and migration toward boundaries. | Safety responsibility without resource/stop authority is invalid. | S062; S081; S082; S085 |
| Authority and accountability | Assign authority matching responsibility; preserve named decision accountability. | Systems explanation must not erase deliberate misconduct or competence obligations. | S012; S112 |
| Reporting / just culture | Protect good-faith weak-signal reporting and separate learning from inappropriate blame. | Counts remain incentive-dependent; privacy/security/accountability boundaries remain. | S080; S112; S116 |
| Organisational learning | Recommendations need a causal mechanism, capable owner and effectiveness check. | Report completion is not control closure. | S076; S078; S079 |
| Safety culture | Translate broad culture claims into observable control, incentive, reporting and resource mechanisms. | Generic survey score is not direct safety evidence. | S071; S072 |
| Contractor/supplier boundaries | Retain integrator accountability, interface assumptions, evidence and change notification. | Responsibility cannot be transferred without actual control and observability. | S012; S042; S052 |
| Adaptation/resilience | Permit adaptation inside explicit hazard/authority envelopes with fallback and recovery. | Do not romanticise workarounds or use resilience language without a decision model. | S069; S070; S111 |


The model is neither blame-free nor blame-centred. It distinguishes **causal explanation**, **control authority**, **competence/duty**, **deliberate misconduct**, **fair reporting** and **corrective action**. “Systemic” does not mean nobody is accountable; “operator error” does not mean the system is explained.

| Safety review board | Authorised challenge and acceptance of consequential safety decisions. | Concentrates competence, cross-boundary authority and dissent resolution. | Rubber stamps, meets without evidence, duplicates work or has no authority. | Context dependent. | Named risk owner plus independent challenge, integrated design review or regulator/operator decision path. | Use only where consequence/conflict/independence justify a standing or ad hoc forum. |
| Risk matrix | Explicit consequence, uncertainty and prioritisation dialogue. | Can provide a shared coarse vocabulary. | Ordinal arithmetic, calibration failure, category gaming and colour-as-truth. | No. | Direct constraints, narrative uncertainty, quantitative/sensitivity analysis or consequence-first tiers. | Do not adopt score-as-risk; ESS-019/020 survive, ESS-055 rejected. |
| Safety case | Claims connected to current evidence, assumptions, uncertainty and decision authority. | Makes reasoning visible and challengeable. | After-the-fact narrative, stale configuration, confirmation bias and document completion. | No prescribed format. | Modular assurance graph, decision record, evidence bundle or compact rationale. | Retain ESS-026/027/030; reject complete-case-equals-safe ESS-062. |

| FMEA worksheet | Structured search over component/function failure modes, effects and controls. | Finds failure-driven design, diagnostic and maintenance issues. | Mechanical row completion, generic modes and no system/interface reasoning. | No. | Design review table, model-based FMEA, fault injection or targeted checklist. | Retain ESS-005 as complement; reject universality. |
| Fault tree diagram | Explicit top-down causal logic and dependencies for a defined top event. | Exposes cut sets, common paths and sensitivity. | Omitted events/dependence, static logic and quantification beyond evidence. | No. | Boolean model, causal graph, formal state model or concise argument. | Retain ESS-006 within scope; supplement interactions and uncertainty. |
| HAZOP workshop / guideword sheet | Disciplined multidisciplinary deviation search and action closure. | Surfaces process/intention deviations using operating expertise. | Workshop fatigue, guideword ritual, overbroad nodes and recommendation lists. | No. | Focused deviation review, procedure/software HAZOP, scenario review. | Retain ESS-007 when process semantics fit; tailor depth. |
| STPA control-structure diagram | Explicit controllers, processes, actions, constraints, feedback and unsafe interactions. | Reveals nonfailure, software, timing and authority hazards. | Diagram explosion, subjective boundaries and no design consumer. | No. | State/control table, interface contract model, causal graph or other interaction representation. | Retain ESS-008–011; reject STPA universal replacement ESS-067. |
| Certification checklist | Coverage of domain objectives and public/independent governance. | Coordinates minimum evidence and responsibilities. | Objective completion substitutes for current system truth or scope is forgotten. | Domain specific. | Objective-based assurance, direct evidence plus regulator decision, change-aware case. | Certification remains bounded evidence; ESS-057 rejected. |
| Independent-review signature | Independently informative challenge and evidence. | Can expose conflict, common blind spots and weak premises. | Shared source/oracle, ceremonial sign-off, late duplication. | No. | Evidence-dependence review, targeted IV&V, dissent record, independent test. | Retain ESS-025/031; reject count/signature proxy ESS-061. |
| Safety-culture survey | Diagnostic information about reporting, incentives, authority and work conditions. | May surface perceptions and local variation. | Composite score treated as safety evidence, benchmark gaming and no hazard link. | No. | Mixed-method work observation, control/authority indicators, protected reporting. | Survey may be one input; ESS-065 rejects score-as-control. |
| Incident-rate dashboard | Operational outcome evidence interpreted with exposure and reporting context. | Can identify trends in common events. | Zero targets suppress reporting; rare-event silence looks safe. | No. | Barrier/precursor/control-health indicators plus protected incident/near-miss learning. | Retain ESS-039/042; reject ESS-058. |
| Alarm / dashboard alert | Timely hazard-state feedback to an authorised consumer. | Enables preventive or containment action. | No action, poor discrimination, alert flood and alarm fatigue. | Only if needed. | Direct interlock, periodic inspection, exception report or adaptive prioritisation. | Retain ESS-034 only with signal/action/burden performance. |

| Change-control form | Affected-scope safety impact, authority, evidence reuse and rollback. | Prevents silent invalidation of controls/assumptions. | File-count classification, blanket process, stale approvals and workaround. | No. | Diff-linked impact graph, automated dependency check, direct regression gate or risk owner decision. | Retain ESS-028/029; reject maximal process ESS-056. |
| Corrective-action database | Owner, causal mechanism, implementation and effectiveness/recurrence verification. | Makes unresolved recommendations visible. | Status gaming, action inflation and closure on document delivery. | No. | Work item with proof condition, design change plus monitor, regulator recommendation system. | Retain ESS-041 and live consumer ESS-048. |
| Resilience workshop / score | Bounded adaptation, recovery and operational-envelope capacity. | Can reveal how work handles variability and surprise. | Vague capacity language, retrospective success stories and no constraint/authority. | No. | Hazard-specific envelope, degraded-mode/recovery test and runtime assurance. | Generic ESS-068 remains contested; specific ESS-036/037/045 survive. |


## EVOLVED_SYSTEMS_SAFETY_CRITICISM_LEDGER

| CRITICISM | TARGET CLASS | EVIDENCE BASIS | EVOLUTION STATUS | SURVIVING BOUNDARY | SOURCES |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Component-centric analysis misses unsafe interactions. | UNDERLYING_PROPERTY / ANALYSIS_TECHNIQUE | Ariane, Therac, Uber, 737 MAX and STAMP literature show loss without a simple random component-failure explanation. | GENERALIZED / HYBRIDISED | Retain failure analysis but add system interaction/control/interface reasoning. | S017; S018; S083; S084; S088; S089 |
| FMEA can become mechanical row completion. | ANALYSIS_TECHNIQUE / CEREMONY | Standards define bounded technique semantics; process critiques show generic lists and action failure. | REFINED / NARROWED | Hazard-relevant scope, credible modes/effects and action closure; use complements. | S007; S038 |
| Fault trees omit unknown, dynamic, software or organisational interactions. | ANALYSIS_TECHNIQUE | FTA’s top-event/event logic is powerful but model-bounded; systems literature supplies omitted classes. | PRESERVED / HYBRIDISED | Use within represented logic, expose dependencies/uncertainty and complement with scenario/control methods. | S008; S009; S017; S109 |
| Risk matrices are inconsistent and falsely precise. | RISK_QUANTIFICATION / PROXY_OR_COMPLIANCE_GAMING | Mathematical analyses show ranking reversal, range compression and ordinal-arithmetic defects; HSE documents pitfalls. | REJECTED_AS_TRUTH / NARROWED_AS_AID | Separate consequence and uncertainty; use scores only as transparent non-dispositive prompts. | S036; S037; S038 |
| Rare-event probabilities are unsupported by data. | RISK_QUANTIFICATION | PRA guidance requires model/data/uncertainty discipline; catastrophic evidence is sparse and dependent. | REFINED / STILL_CONTESTED | State epistemic limits, sensitivity and alternatives; use constraints/monitoring where quantification cannot decide. | S039; S040; S041 |
| SIL, ASIL and DAL are read as direct probabilities of total safety. | CERTIFICATION_ARTEFACT / DOMAIN_MISAPPLICATION | Functional and development-assurance standards attach objectives to functions/failure conditions, not universal system truth. | NARROWED | Use hazard-derived graded rigour within domain scope and complement interaction/intended-function analyses. | S021; S023; S024; S025; S029 |
| Hazard logs go stale and reward entry count. | EVIDENCE_STALENESS / CEREMONY | Nimrod and living-assurance work show document/system divergence; lifecycle standards require current tracking. | REFINED | Configuration-aware current hazard/control/decision state with ownership and retirement. | S012; S042; S047; S048 |
| Safety cases become paperwork and confirmation bias. | CERTIFICATION_ARTEFACT / ORGANISATIONAL_IMPLEMENTATION | Nimrod is direct evidence; assurance-case scholars identify argument/evidence/confidence limits. | REFINED / HYBRIDISED | Living, defeater-led, provenance-aware cases tied to a live decision. | S044; S045; S046; S047; S048; S108 |

## EVOLVED_SYSTEMS_SAFETY_CONSEQUENCE_REVERSIBILITY_PROFILES

The full profile is present for every property in the ledger. The table below cross-indexes all 54 admitted/contextual properties and makes the anti-over-control boundary visible.

| PROPERTY | CONSEQUENCE | REVERSIBILITY | COUPLING | OBSERVABILITY LATENCY | RECOVERY DIFFICULTY | CONTROL-STRENGTH RELATION | CHEAP PATH | OVER-CONTROL FAILURE | MATURE FORM |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ESS-001 — Explicit unacceptable-loss framing | Control depth increases with credible harm to people, mission, environment, critical service or public exposure. | More assurance is warranted where effects cannot be cheaply rolled back or compensated. | Tighter coupling and broader propagation increase the value of explicit modelling and containment. | Longer delay between unsafe action and observable consequence increases anticipatory analysis needs. | Difficult or ethically impossible recovery/testing increases dependence on analytical and independent evidence. | Scale analysis, independence, evidence and recovery controls to consequence and uncertainty, not to labels. | For trivial reversible work, state the bounded loss in one line and use the authoritative deterministic check; no elaborate taxonomy. | Uniform maximal treatment wastes scarce safety attention and can provoke workarounds or unavailable service. | A concise, current, decision-linked definition of unacceptable loss that bounds later analysis without pretending completeness. |
| ESS-002 — Hazardous system-state framing distinct from failure | Control depth increases with credible harm to people, mission, environment, critical service or public exposure. | More assurance is warranted where effects cannot be cheaply rolled back or compensated. | Tighter coupling and broader propagation increase the value of explicit modelling and containment. | Longer delay between unsafe action and observable consequence increases anticipatory analysis needs. | Difficult or ethically impossible recovery/testing increases dependence on analytical and independent evidence. | Scale analysis, independence, evidence and recovery controls to consequence and uncertainty, not to labels. | A simple local task with a complete deterministic invariant may use that invariant directly rather than a separate hazard ontology. | Uniform maximal treatment wastes scarce safety attention and can provoke workarounds or unavailable service. | A current loss-linked hazardous-state model with explicit boundary, exposure and causal assumptions. |
| ESS-003 — Enforceable safety constraints | Control depth increases with credible harm to people, mission, environment, critical service or public exposure. | More assurance is warranted where effects cannot be cheaply rolled back or compensated. | Tighter coupling and broader propagation increase the value of explicit modelling and containment. | Longer delay between unsafe action and observable consequence increases anticipatory analysis needs. | Difficult or ethically impossible recovery/testing increases dependence on analytical and independent evidence. | Scale analysis, independence, evidence and recovery controls to consequence and uncertainty, not to labels. | Where a deterministic existing rule already proves the safe condition, record/reuse it rather than create duplicate safety requirements. | Uniform maximal treatment wastes scarce safety attention and can provoke workarounds or unavailable service. | The minimum sufficient constraint is explicit, allocated, enforceable, verified and paired with feedback or bounded assurance. |
| ESS-004 — Lifecycle hazard identification with explicit completeness boundaries | Control depth increases with credible harm to people, mission, environment, critical service or public exposure. | More assurance is warranted where effects cannot be cheaply rolled back or compensated. | Tighter coupling and broader propagation increase the value of explicit modelling and containment. | Longer delay between unsafe action and observable consequence increases anticipatory analysis needs. | Difficult or ethically impossible recovery/testing increases dependence on analytical and independent evidence. | Scale analysis, independence, evidence and recovery controls to consequence and uncertainty, not to labels. | Low-consequence reversible work needs only a bounded check of known hazards and the deterministic discriminator, not a comprehensive workshop. | Uniform maximal treatment wastes scarce safety attention and can provoke workarounds or unavailable service. | Claim bounded coverage over a declared population; never claim that all possible hazards are known. |
| ESS-005 — Component failure-effects analysis as a bounded complement | Control depth increases with credible harm to people, mission, environment, critical service or public exposure. | More assurance is warranted where effects cannot be cheaply rolled back or compensated. | Tighter coupling and broader propagation increase the value of explicit modelling and containment. | Longer delay between unsafe action and observable consequence increases anticipatory analysis needs. | Difficult or ethically impossible recovery/testing increases dependence on analytical and independent evidence. | Scale analysis, independence, evidence and recovery controls to consequence and uncertainty, not to labels. | Skip a full worksheet where the component is non-safety-significant, trivially replaceable, or a validated deterministic test already exhausts the relevant failure set. | Uniform maximal treatment wastes scarce safety attention and can provoke workarounds or unavailable service. | Use FMEA for what it represents well; do not treat a completed FMEA as a complete system-safety analysis. |
| ESS-006 — Top-down causal-path and logical analysis | Control depth increases with credible harm to people, mission, environment, critical service or public exposure. | More assurance is warranted where effects cannot be cheaply rolled back or compensated. | Tighter coupling and broader propagation increase the value of explicit modelling and containment. | Longer delay between unsafe action and observable consequence increases anticipatory analysis needs. | Difficult or ethically impossible recovery/testing increases dependence on analytical and independent evidence. | Scale analysis, independence, evidence and recovery controls to consequence and uncertainty, not to labels. | For a simple deterministic invariant, use direct proof/test; do not construct a tree that merely restates the invariant. | Uniform maximal treatment wastes scarce safety attention and can provoke workarounds or unavailable service. | Use top-down logic where the event structure is meaningful; pair it with other searches for unmodelled interactions and organisational causes. |
| ESS-007 — Structured process-deviation search | Control depth increases with credible harm to people, mission, environment, critical service or public exposure. | More assurance is warranted where effects cannot be cheaply rolled back or compensated. | Tighter coupling and broader propagation increase the value of explicit modelling and containment. | Longer delay between unsafe action and observable consequence increases anticipatory analysis needs. | Difficult or ethically impossible recovery/testing increases dependence on analytical and independent evidence. | Scale analysis, independence, evidence and recovery controls to consequence and uncertainty, not to labels. | Do not convene a full HAZOP for a tiny reversible change with a complete change discriminator; use focused review. | Uniform maximal treatment wastes scarce safety attention and can provoke workarounds or unavailable service. | Structured deviation prompts plus empowered expertise and action closure; method depth proportional to hazard and change. |
| ESS-008 — Unsafe interaction and unsafe-control analysis | Control depth increases with credible harm to people, mission, environment, critical service or public exposure. | More assurance is warranted where effects cannot be cheaply rolled back or compensated. | Tighter coupling and broader propagation increase the value of explicit modelling and containment. | Longer delay between unsafe action and observable consequence increases anticipatory analysis needs. | Difficult or ethically impossible recovery/testing increases dependence on analytical and independent evidence. | Scale analysis, independence, evidence and recovery controls to consequence and uncertainty, not to labels. | Where a simple component failure fully determines the hazard, use the cheaper failure analysis and direct control; do not force a control diagram. | Uniform maximal treatment wastes scarce safety attention and can provoke workarounds or unavailable service. | Explicitly reason about unsafe composition and control context, using the cheapest adequate representation and complementary techniques. |
| ESS-009 — Closed-loop control and feedback integrity | Control depth increases with credible harm to people, mission, environment, critical service or public exposure. | More assurance is warranted where effects cannot be cheaply rolled back or compensated. | Tighter coupling and broader propagation increase the value of explicit modelling and containment. | Longer delay between unsafe action and observable consequence increases anticipatory analysis needs. | Difficult or ethically impossible recovery/testing increases dependence on analytical and independent evidence. | Scale analysis, independence, evidence and recovery controls to consequence and uncertainty, not to labels. | For local directly observable reversible actions, immediate observation/test can serve as the feedback path without additional instrumentation. | Uniform maximal treatment wastes scarce safety attention and can provoke workarounds or unavailable service. | Every consequential control has evidence sufficient to establish intended state, or the system treats state as unknown and constrains operation. |
| ESS-010 — Controller process-model and mode consistency | Control depth increases with credible harm to people, mission, environment, critical service or public exposure. | More assurance is warranted where effects cannot be cheaply rolled back or compensated. | Tighter coupling and broader propagation increase the value of explicit modelling and containment. | Longer delay between unsafe action and observable consequence increases anticipatory analysis needs. | Difficult or ethically impossible recovery/testing increases dependence on analytical and independent evidence. | Scale analysis, independence, evidence and recovery controls to consequence and uncertainty, not to labels. | A stateless local action with directly visible conditions may require only a simple precondition check. | Uniform maximal treatment wastes scarce safety attention and can provoke workarounds or unavailable service. | Make safety-relevant process-model assumptions visible, monitored and fail-bounded. |
| ESS-011 — Timing, ordering, duration and transition semantics | Control depth increases with credible harm to people, mission, environment, critical service or public exposure. | More assurance is warranted where effects cannot be cheaply rolled back or compensated. | Tighter coupling and broader propagation increase the value of explicit modelling and containment. | Longer delay between unsafe action and observable consequence increases anticipatory analysis needs. | Difficult or ethically impossible recovery/testing increases dependence on analytical and independent evidence. | Scale analysis, independence, evidence and recovery controls to consequence and uncertainty, not to labels. | A synchronous local operation with atomic deterministic semantics may need only a direct timeout/completion check. | Uniform maximal treatment wastes scarce safety attention and can provoke workarounds or unavailable service. | Apply temporal rigour where timing can change safety; use direct atomic checks where it cannot. |
